title: Learning Platform Operations & Migration Readiness
summary: I supported the transition from Absorb LMS to Docebo LMS by testing how migrated courses, learning plans, certifications, renewals, visibility, navigation, and support workflows behaved across employee, partner, and customer experiences.

content.business_need: Move a working learning ecosystem from Absorb LMS into Docebo LMS while preserving or rebuilding course visibility, catalogs, learning plans, certifications, renewals, content relationships, learner navigation, support guidance, and reporting expectations.
content.audience: Employees, partners, customers, and learning operations teams.
learning_objectives: Validate how learner-facing catalogs, learning plans, certifications, renewal paths, navigation, and content translated from Absorb into Docebo before launch.
Test employee, partner, and customer experiences from a learner point of view in Docebo.
Identify content mapping, duplicate-content, visibility, and relationship issues before they reached learners.
Document issues, support retesting, and contribute to launch-readiness and learner-support work.
content.role: Instructional designer and LMS content administrator supporting the Absorb-to-Docebo migration, UAT, learner-experience validation, and launch readiness.
content.design_approach: I treated the migration as both a platform change and a learner-experience change. I used my knowledge of the existing Absorb learning ecosystem as a baseline, then tested what learners could see and do in Docebo, checked the structures behind those journeys, documented issues, and worked with the broader migration team to validate fixes before and after launch.
content.development_process: I participated in UAT for employee, partner, and customer experiences; validated migrated catalogs, learning plans, certifications, renewals, thumbnails, navigation, and learner-facing content in Docebo; surfaced mapping, duplicate-content, and visibility issues; reviewed learner guidance; and supported issue triage, retesting, and launch readiness.
outcomes: Used the existing Absorb LMS experience as a baseline for validating how learning content and learner journeys translated into Docebo LMS.
Tested employee, partner, and customer learner experiences in Docebo across learning plans, certifications, renewals, catalogs, visibility, navigation, and learner-facing content.
Documented issues, helped validate fixes, and supported migration readiness and post-launch issue triage.

detail_sections.title: What I tested in Docebo before and around launch.
detail_sections.summary: I checked learner-facing behavior and the platform structures behind it using the existing Absorb experience as a baseline.

items.title: Audience visibility
items.body: Tested employee, partner, and customer experiences and checked whether migrated content appeared to the right audiences in Docebo.

items.title: Learning plans
items.body: Reviewed how learning-plan structure, relationships, and learner-facing behavior translated from Absorb into Docebo.

items.title: Certifications + renewals
items.body: Tested certification workflows and renewal paths so new and returning learners followed the intended experience.

items.title: Content + navigation
items.body: Validated learner-facing content, thumbnails, navigation, catalogs, and supporting materials for Docebo launch readiness.

items.title: Issue triage
items.body: Documented problems, supported troubleshooting, and helped move migration issues through retesting and resolution.

detail_sections.title: What I looked for when Absorb behavior did not translate cleanly into Docebo.
detail_sections.summary: The migration created new structures and relationships that needed active comparison and validation.
rows: Whether migrated content was connected to the intended learning structure in Docebo.
Incorrect mapping could break the learner journey or completion logic.
Overlapping or repeated records created during transition work.
Duplicates could confuse learners and administrators.
Which audiences could see catalogs, training, and learning structures.
The right content had to appear to the right learner group.
How certification and renewal paths behaved for returning learners.
Renewal logic needed to preserve a clear repeat-learning experience.
Navigation, onboarding guidance, and support resources in the new LMS.
A technically correct migration still needed to be understandable to learners.
detail_sections.note: This is a public-safe reconstruction. Internal configuration, learner records, issue logs, and proprietary screenshots are omitted.

detail_sections.title: What the Absorb-to-Docebo migration reinforced for me.
detail_sections.summary: LMS migrations depend on governance, testing, and learner communication as much as configuration.

items.title: Test by role
items.body: Employee, partner, and customer experiences need to be tested as different learner journeys rather than assumed to behave the same way.

items.title: Compare behavior, not just files
items.body: A course existing in Docebo did not mean the migration was finished; visibility, relationships, renewals, tracking, and navigation still needed validation.

items.title: Treat support as part of launch
items.body: Learner guidance and support resources matter because a technically correct platform change can still be confusing to use.
